'''Jiang Mianheng''' ({{lang-zh|s=江绵恒}}; born 8 April 1951) is a Chinese scholar, entrepreneur, and political figure. He has served as vice president of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] and president of [[ShanghaiTech University]]. His father was [[Jiang Zemin]], [[General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party|general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party]] from 1989 to 2002.

==Biography==

Jiang earned a Ph.D. in Material Science<ref>https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Xnix9cvMbQ0</ref> from [[Drexel University]] in 1991 with a dissertation titled ''Point contact tunneling study of the high transition temperature superconductor Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>CaCu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8</sub>'' in 1991.<ref>[http://english.cas.cn/eng2003/news/detailnewsb.asp?InfoNo=20986 Chinese Academy of Sciences] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070626163433/http://english.cas.cn/eng2003/news/detailnewsb.asp?InfoNo=20986|date=2007-06-26 }}</ref>

Jiang also served as one of the head researchers for the [[Chinese space program]]. In 2007, he failed to win nomination as a delegate to the [[17th National Congress of the Communist Party of China|17th Party Congress]].

He served as one of the vice presidents in the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]  until November 2011.<ref>[http://english.cas.cn/eng2003/page/MA_02.htm#vice] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080803072627/http://english.cas.cn/eng2003/page/MA_02.htm#vice|date=August 3, 2008}}</ref><ref>Singtao news 11-19-2011 section A2. 不再擔任江綿恆去向有玄機.</ref> Then he became president of the academy's Shanghai branch until 2015.<ref name="UWN">{{cite web |url=http://www.universityworldnews.com/article.php?story=20140309162305896|title='Princeling' named head of new Shanghai university |author-first1=Mimi|author-last1=Leung|author-first2=Yojana|author-last2=Sharma|date=9 March 2014 |website=[[University World News]] |access-date=29 May 2014|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150517162050/http://www.universityworldnews.com/article.php?story=20140309162305896|archive-date=17 May 2015}}</ref> In 2014 he was appointed president of the newly established [[ShanghaiTech University]].<ref name="UWN" />

Jiang has headed a number of national research programs in alternative energy and other technologies: "coal liquefaction, electric cars, mobile phone networks, particle accelerators, spaceships, lunar satellites and [[Molten salt reactor#Chinese project|liquid fluoride thorium reactor]]."<ref>{{cite web |title=Jiang's son loses out in bid for top science post  |url=https://www.scmp.com/article/739927/jiangs-son-loses-out-bid-top-science-post |website=South China Morning Post |date=5 March 2011 |access-date=29 October 2021}}</ref>

Jiang is a co-founder of the [[Shanghai]]-based Grace Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation, which gained some coverage in the American press for their employment of [[Bush family]] member [[Neil Bush]] as a general consultant.<ref>{{cite news|last=Clendenin|first=Mike|title=China foundry's expansion plans may include IPO|url=http://www.eetimes.com/General/PrintView/4047135|accessdate=27 February 2013|newspaper=EE Times|date=12 February 2004}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2003-11-26|title=Bush's younger brother quizzed over $2m deal|url=https://www.smh.com.au/world/bushs-younger-brother-quizzed-over-2m-deal-20031126-gdhuyc.html|access-date=2022-01-30|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en}}</ref>
